docs.title: bbui
docs.text: bbui is a command-line Ansible inventory manager. It supports YAML and INI formats, the BlueBanquise layout, and a git-like staging workflow.

docs.title: Features
docs.text: Feature Description Multi-format Read and write YAML and INI inventories BlueBanquise Layout and group rules enforced automatically Staging Changes are never written without an explicit commit NodeSet Host range expressions (c[001:100]) via ClusterShell Dot-notation Inspect nested variables (bmc.ip4, disks[0].name)

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
# Install
poetry install

# List hosts in an inventory
bbcli host list -I ./my-inventory/

# Add hosts (BlueBanquise layout)
bbcli host add 'c[001:010]' --groups fn_compute,hw_typeA,os_ubuntu -I ./my-inventory/

# Review what will be written
bbcli pending -I ./my-inventory/

# Write to disk
bbcli commit -I ./my-inventory/

docs.title: Global options
docs.text:
All commands accept these two options:

Option Short Env Description --inventory PATH -i BBUI_INVENTORY Single inventory file (YAML or INI). Writes immediately. --inventory-dir PATH -I BBUI_INVENTORY_DIR Inventory directory. Enables the staging workflow.

When --inventory-dir is used, changes are staged and require a bbcli commit to be persisted.

docs.title: bbcli host add <nodeset>
docs.text:
Stages the addition of one or more hosts. Supports NodeSet syntax.

bbcli host add web01 -I ./inventory/
bbcli host add 'web[01:10]' --groups webservers,staging -I ./inventory/
bbcli host add 'c[001:100]' --groups fn_compute,hw_typeA,os_ubuntu -I ./inventory/
Option Short Description --groups LIST -g Comma-separated list of groups to assign to the hosts

BlueBanquise layout: the three prefixes fn_*, hw_*, os_* are mandatory. A host that already exists is silently skipped.

docs.title: bbcli host remove <hostname>
docs.text:
Stages the removal of a host.

bbcli host remove web05 -I ./inventory/

docs.title: bbcli host list
docs.text:
Lists all hosts, their groups, and their variables. If changes are staged, the staged view is shown (with a warning).

bbcli host list -I ./inventory/

┌─ Hosts ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Name  │ Groups                          │ Vars               │
│ c001  │ fn_compute, hw_typeA, os_ubuntu │                    │
│ mgt1  │ fn_management, hw_typeC, os_rhel│ {'ip': '10.0.0.1'} │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: bbcli host show <nodeset> [varname]
docs.text:
Shows details and variables for one or more hosts.

# Full details for a single host
bbcli host show web01 -I ./inventory/

# Details for multiple hosts via NodeSet
bbcli host show 'web[01:05]' -I ./inventory/

# Show a single variable across a range of hosts
bbcli host show 'c[001:010]' bmc.ip4 -I ./inventory/
bbcli host show 'c[001:010]' disks[0].name -I ./inventory/

In single-variable mode, the output is a compact Host | Value table. In full mode, each host is shown in its own block with variables in dot-notation.

docs.title: bbcli group add <name>
docs.text:
Stages the addition of a group.

bbcli group add storage -I ./inventory/

docs.title: bbcli group remove <name>
docs.text:
Stages the removal of a group.

bbcli group remove storage -I ./inventory/

docs.title: bbcli group list
docs.text:
Lists all groups with their hosts (folded NodeSet) and child groups.

bbcli group list -I ./inventory/

┌─ Groups ──────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Name            │ Hosts        │ Children          │
│ fn_compute      │ c[001:004]   │                   │
│ fn_management   │ mgt[1:2]     │                   │
│ hw_cpu_type_A   │ c[001:004]   │                   │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: bbcli group show <name>
docs.text:
Shows details of a group: hosts, child groups, and variables.

bbcli group show webservers -I ./inventory/

docs.title: bbcli vars show <varname>
docs.text:
Shows every host and group that defines <varname>, with its value and source file. Supports dot-notation for nested values.

# Simple variable
bbcli vars show ansible_user -I ./inventory/

# Nested variable
bbcli vars show network.ip -I ./inventory/
bbcli vars show bmc.ip4 -I ./inventory/

# List element
bbcli vars show disks[0].name -I ./inventory/

# Filters
bbcli vars show ansible_user -I ./inventory/ --hosts   # hosts only
bbcli vars show ntp_server   -I ./inventory/ --groups  # groups only
Option Short Description --hosts -H Show only host matches --groups -G Show only group matches

Example output:

         Variable: ansible_user
┌───────┬────────────┬────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Kind  │ Owner      │ Value  │ Source file                           │
│ host  │ web01      │ ubuntu │ inventory/cluster/nodes/web.yml       │
│ host  │ web02      │ ubuntu │ inventory/cluster/nodes/web.yml       │
│ group │ webservers │ deploy │ inventory/group_vars/webservers.yml   │
└───────┴────────────┴────────┴──────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Dot-notation syntax
docs.text: Value type Format Example Scalar key ansible_user Nested dict key.sub network.ip Deep dict key.sub1.sub2 interfaces.eth0.speed List element key[i] dns_servers[0] Key in list key[i].sub disks[0].name

docs.title: bbcli pending
docs.text:
Shows staged changes and the files that will be written on the next commit.

bbcli pending -I ./inventory/

Requires --inventory-dir.

docs.title: bbcli commit
docs.text:
Writes all staged changes to disk and clears the staging cache.

bbcli commit -I ./inventory/

Requires --inventory-dir.

docs.title: bbcli discard
docs.text:
Drops all staged changes without writing to disk.

bbcli discard -I ./inventory/          # asks for confirmation
bbcli discard -I ./inventory/ --force  # no confirmation
Option Short Description --force -f Skip confirmation prompt

Requires --inventory-dir.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Dependency Version Python 3.14+ ClusterShell ^1.9 Poetry For development

ClusterShell is installed automatically by Poetry.

docs.title: From the repository
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/samgrcia/bbui.git
cd bbui
poetry install

Verify:

poetry run bbcli --help

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Instead of passing --inventory or --inventory-dir on every command, you can export them:

export BBUI_INVENTORY_DIR=/path/to/my-inventory
bbcli host list          # equivalent to bbcli host list -I /path/to/my-inventory
Variable Equivalent option Description BBUI_INVENTORY --inventory / -i Path to a single inventory file BBUI_INVENTORY_DIR --inventory-dir / -I Inventory directory (enables staging)

When both are set, --inventory-dir / BBUI_INVENTORY_DIR takes precedence.

docs.title: Inventory layouts
docs.text: bbui supports two layouts: a generic Ansible layout and the structured BlueBanquise layout. Detection is automatic on every command.

docs.title: Generic layout
docs.text:
A directory containing any mix of YAML and INI files.

inventory/
├── hosts.yml           # hosts in YAML
├── staging.ini         # hosts in INI
└── group_vars/
    ├── all.yml         # vars applied to all groups
    ├── webservers.yml  # vars for group "webservers"
    └── databases/      # vars for "databases" (directory layout)
        ├── main.yml
        └── secrets.yml

Files are loaded alphabetically; last-writer-wins on conflicts. group_vars/ is applied last, matching Ansible's own precedence rules.

docs.title: YAML format
docs.text:
all:
  children:
    webservers:
      hosts:
        web01:
          ansible_user: ubuntu
        web02:

docs.title: INI format
docs.text:
[webservers]
web01 ansible_user=ubuntu
web02

[webservers:vars]
ansible_become=true

[production:children]
webservers

:vars and :children sections are supported.

docs.title: BlueBanquise layout
docs.text:
bbui automatically detects the BlueBanquise layout as soon as the directory passed to -I contains cluster/nodes/ or cluster/groups/.

Important: always point -I at the parent of cluster/, not at cluster/ itself.

inventory-root/           ← pass this path to -I
├── cluster/
│   ├── nodes/
│   │   ├── compute.yml   # fn_compute hosts + their vars
│   │   ├── login.yml     # fn_login hosts + their vars
│   │   └── management.yml
│   └── groups/
│       ├── fn            # fn_* group declarations (INI, no extension)
│       ├── hw            # hw_* group declarations
│       ├── os            # os_* group declarations
│       └── others        # user-defined groups (default bucket)
└── group_vars/
    └── ...

docs.title: Mandatory group membership
docs.text:
Every host must belong to exactly one group from each of the three base prefixes:

Prefix Purpose Examples fn_ Function (functional role) fn_compute, fn_management, fn_login hw_ Hardware type hw_cpu_server_type_A, hw_gpu_type_B os_ Operating system os_ubuntu_24, os_rhel_9 
# Correct — all three prefixes present
bbcli host add 'c[001:010]' --groups fn_compute,hw_typeA,os_ubuntu -I ./inventory-root/

# Error — missing hw_* group
bbcli host add c011 --groups fn_compute,os_ubuntu -I ./inventory-root/

# Error — two fn_* groups
bbcli host add c012 --groups fn_compute,fn_login,hw_typeA,os_ubuntu -I ./inventory-root/

docs.title: Node files (cluster/nodes/)
docs.text:
Each node file is a standard Ansible YAML file with all as the root key:

all:
  hosts:
    c001:
      bmc_ip: 10.0.0.1
    c002:
  • Existing hosts are written back to the file they were loaded from.
  • New hosts are co-located with existing peers of the same fn_* group (alphabetically first peer file wins).
  • If no peer exists yet, a new <fn_suffix>.yml file is created.

docs.title: Group files (cluster/groups/)
docs.text:
Group files use INI format (no extension). Hosts appear as Ansible NodeSet expressions (node[01:10]) rather than one per line.

[fn_compute]
c[001:004]

[fn_management]
mgt[1:2]
  • fn_*, hw_*, and os_* groups are always written to their canonical files (fn, hw, os).
  • User-defined groups loaded from a named file are written back to that same file.
  • User-defined groups created from scratch go to cluster/groups/others.

docs.title: Cache
docs.text:
bbui maintains two caches under <inventory-root>/.bbui/:

File Purpose inventory_cache.pkl Parsed inventory (read cache). Invalidated when any source file is newer. cache.pkl Staged mutations. Present only between stage and commit / discard.

Caches are automatically invalidated when the layout type changes (e.g. after migrating to the BlueBanquise layout).

docs.title: NodeSet syntax
docs.text: bbui uses ClusterShell to handle host range expressions. Two syntaxes coexist: ClusterShell syntax (CLI commands) and Ansible syntax (INI files).

docs.title: ClusterShell syntax (CLI commands)
docs.text:
Any command that accepts a hostname also accepts a NodeSet expression.

Expression Expands to web01 web01 web[01:10] web01 … web10 web[01-10] web01 … web10 (dash, synonym for : in ClusterShell) web[01:10/2] web01, web03, web05 … (step of 2) web[01:10],db[1:5] union of both ranges web[01:10]!web05 exclusion of web05 c[001:100] c001 … c100 (zero-padding preserved) 
# Add 10 nodes at once
bbcli host add 'c[001:010]' --groups fn_compute,hw_typeA,os_ubuntu -I ./inventory/

# Show a variable across a range of hosts
bbcli host show 'c[001:004]' bmc.ip4 -I ./inventory/

docs.title: Ansible syntax (INI files)
docs.text:
In INI files generated by bbui, ranges use the : separator (Ansible standard). The - separator (ClusterShell) is not recognised by Ansible.

[fn_compute]
c[001:004]
g[001:002]

[fn_management]
mgt[1:2]

bbui converts automatically on write: node[01-03] (ClusterShell) → node[01:03] (Ansible).

docs.title: Fold and expand
docs.text:
Operation Input Output Expand c[001:003] ['c001', 'c002', 'c003'] Fold ['c001', 'c002', 'c003'] c[001:003]

Non-contiguous nodes are separated by a comma:

['web01', 'web03']   →  web[01,03]
['web01', 'db01']    →  db01,web01   (distinct groups → two lines in INI)

In INI files, each top-level group from the folded expression is written on its own line:

[my_group]
db01
web[01,03]

docs.title: Staging workflow
docs.text:
bbui uses a git-inspired staging system: changes accumulate in memory and are never written to disk without an explicit commit.

Staging is enabled as soon as you use --inventory-dir / -I. With --inventory / -i (single file), changes are written immediately.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
bbcli host add 'c[011:020]' --groups fn_compute,hw_typeA,os_ubuntu -I ./inventory/
      │
      ▼
  [staging cache]   ←  inventory_cache.pkl (read) + cache.pkl (mutations)
      │
      ├──  bbcli pending   →  preview changes and target files
      │
      ├──  bbcli commit    →  write to disk, clear cache
      │
      └──  bbcli discard   →  drop changes, clear cache

docs.title: The two caches
docs.text:
Both caches live under <inventory-dir>/.bbui/:

File Purpose Lifecycle inventory_cache.pkl Parsed inventory (speeds up successive reads) Invalidated when any source file is newer cache.pkl Staged mutations (modified inventory + change list) Created by stage, deleted by commit or discard

While cache.pkl is present, all read commands (host list, host show, etc.) use it and display a warning that uncommitted changes are active.

docs.title: bbcli pending
docs.text:
Shows staged changes and the files that will be written.

┌─ Pending changes ────────────────────────────────────┐
│   │ Type       │ Nodeset / Subject │ Detail           │
│ + │ host added │ c[011:020]        │ groups=[...]     │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

┌─ Files to be written ──────────────────────────────────┐
│ File                              │ Changes             │
│ inventory/cluster/nodes/nodes.yml │ + c[011:020]        │
│ inventory/cluster/groups/fn       │ + c[011:020]        │
│ inventory/cluster/groups/hw       │ + c[011:020]        │
│ inventory/cluster/groups/os       │ + c[011:020]        │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: bbcli commit
docs.text:
Writes all mutations to disk and deletes cache.pkl.

In BlueBanquise layout, each host is written back to the file it was loaded from. New hosts are co-located with existing peers of the same fn_* group.

bbcli commit -I ./inventory/
# ✓ inventory/cluster/nodes/nodes.yml  (10 change(s))
# ✓ inventory/cluster/groups/fn        (1 change(s))
# Commit complete.

docs.title: bbcli discard
docs.text:
Drops all staged mutations without writing to disk.

bbcli discard -I ./inventory/          # asks for confirmation
bbcli discard -I ./inventory/ --force  # no confirmation

docs.title: Accumulating changes
docs.text:
Multiple successive commands accumulate in the same cache.pkl:

bbcli host add 'c[011:015]' --groups fn_compute,hw_typeA,os_ubuntu -I ./inventory/
bbcli host add 'mgt3'       --groups fn_management,hw_typeC,os_rhel -I ./inventory/
bbcli host remove c005 -I ./inventory/
bbcli pending -I ./inventory/   # shows all 3 changes together
bbcli commit  -I ./inventory/   # writes everything in one pass

docs.title: Read consistency
docs.text:
While cache.pkl is present, read commands (host list, host show, vars show) return the staged state rather than the on-disk state. A warning banner indicates this:

⚠ Showing staged inventory (uncommitted changes present)
